Three API replicas are spread across zones A and B, but every replica authorizes through one zone-A identity endpoint and commits through one zone-A database writer. After zone A fails, why can the zone-B replicas report healthy processes yet complete no bookings, and what must the availability claim state instead?

A team proposes replacing a small self-managed deployment with a managed service because its monthly instance fee is lower. Why can total lifecycle cost still rise, and what must be compared on the same horizon before treating the cheaper fee as evidence?

A new retriever returns several relevant documents that no earlier system retrieved and that the judgment pool never judged. Why can its Recall@k look worse than the system whose results built the pool, and what must be re-run before the two are compared?

A client pages through a list ordered by creation time with a keyset cursor while rows are inserted and one caller's access to a row is revoked. Why does the keyset cursor avoid offset drift without giving a stable snapshot, and what must the cursor bind so a stale page cannot expose the revoked row?

A daily booking total is computed in event time; event E5 arrives after the watermark has closed its window, and a later cancellation must change the total. Why is finalization at the watermark not proof that earlier events are complete, and what must the lateness and correction contract decide before the total is treated as settled?

A proposed index lowers a query's estimated plan cost and the planner chooses an index scan. Why does that not establish lower user latency, and which lifecycle costs decide whether the index is a net improvement?

A team deletes retired customer records from its primary audit store, but a backup archive, a search index and an old incident export still contain them. Why does the primary deletion not satisfy the retention or erasure obligation, and what must the retention design inventory and govern?
Why can three replicas spread across two zones still lose the booking journey together, and what must a recovery test demonstrate beyond healthy processes?

When two simultaneous submissions reuse one idempotency key and the first commits while its response is lost, why is a read-then-insert check insufficient, and what must happen when the key returns with different parameters or after retention ends?
Why does advancing a watermark past a window not make its published total final, and what must the processing contract declare before a late booking correction is applied?
Why can an index that helped one tenant make the same query slower for another, and which conditions must be fixed before the two access paths are compared?
Why can a higher Recall@5 fail to justify a retrieval change, and what must lexical, vector or hybrid candidates share before their ranking metrics are comparable?

Why can a duplicate read sent to a second replica shorten the tail while increasing the load that produced the tail?
Why is R + W > N necessary but not sufficient for a quorum read to return the newest acknowledged write?
Why can an index that helps a uniform workload make the same query slower after one tenant's rows become skewed?
Why must a cached absence or denial be scoped to a principal and a policy revision rather than to an object identifier alone?
Why can a trace set be adequate for diagnosing one slow request yet invalid for estimating how often requests are slow?

Why is an exact nearest-neighbor scan insufficient to certify an approximate index after the embedding model changes?

Why can a read that contacts a quorum of replicas still return a stale value after a write was acknowledged?
Why is telling an assistant to ignore instructions found in retrieved documents insufficient, and where must the boundary be enforced instead?
Why can a query be badly costed when both correlated columns have current statistics, and what has to happen before new extended statistics change the plan?
Why does a failed coordinator leave prepared participants holding locks, and why must one durable decision exist before any participant applies the outcome?
Why can a session token guarantee read-your-writes without making stored data globally consistent, and what must happen when that token cannot survive failover?
Why can a cached not-found keep hiding an object after it has been created, and what must a negative cache key include before a denial may be shared?
Why does one general-purpose API become a poor fit for materially different clients, and what must a per-client backend avoid becoming?
Why must a scatter-gather fix a completeness rule and a straggler policy before it can return an answer, and what must the response disclose about participants that did not reply?
Why does placing a service copy in every region not remove the failover problem, and what must be established before the old regional writer is replaced?

A client sends only the highest commit position it has observed to whichever replica answers. After a leader change, why can a replica whose applied position is numerically higher still return a state that violates read-your-writes, and what must the token and the routing decision carry instead?

A three-voter metadata store is expanded to four voters to improve resilience, and reads and writes continue to use R + W > N. Why does the fourth voter add no failure tolerance while raising the commit quorum, and why can a read still be stale during the membership change?

A shared cache stores a 404 for a document lookup and a 403 for a caller who lacked access. The document is later created and shared with that caller, and the policy revision changes. Why can both cached negatives remain wrong after the change, and what must each key and lifetime bind?

A team replaces a join with an application-maintained index table and adds a covering column so the lookup avoids the base table. Why can the lookup return a stale or wrong row even though the base table is correct, and what must the write path and key preserve?
Every participant votes yes, then the coordinator crashes before recording its decision. Why can no participant safely commit or abort on its own, and what must the recovery decision be based on?

Two client applications share one general-purpose API, and each filters fields and makes several calls. Why can a per-client backend improve the contract without becoming a second domain authority, and what release risk appears when it deploys independently?

A checkout team keeps enlarging its simulation by adding a cache model, a database model and a deployment model, because it assumes that a more detailed model is a more accurate one. Why can the added detail fail to improve the decision, and what test should each proposed addition pass before its verification burden is accepted?

A V12 decision record cites a stable pattern identifier and its canonical owner page, and the derived reverse index lists that pattern next to the decision. What does the link actually establish, and why must it not be read as promotion, validation or a second canonical explanation of the pattern?

A sensitivity screen reports that service mean explains more fitted variance than arrival rate, and the team proposes to cancel the planned service-time measurement because the model already shows what matters. Why is that inference invalid, and what is the ranking legitimately used for?

Two checkout candidates' 95% intervals overlap on success rate, so the review records no difference and keeps the cheaper candidate. Why is that an insufficient-evidence outcome rather than evidence of equivalence, and what must the record state instead?

Candidate A has the lower p95 latency, yet the V12 comparative record recommends candidate B. Why is that not a contradiction, and which part of the recommendation is a value judgment rather than a simulated fact?

A simulation measures a steady-state p95 from a window that starts at time zero, although the model starts empty and its queue fills during the first minutes. Why does that window bias the estimate, what must the scenario declare and the engine enforce about warmup, and why does convergence not repair the bias?
Why does full jitter reduce synchronized retry waves, and why must a model record its jitter policy to be reproducible?
Why does a V12 decision record link one way to existing pattern identifiers instead of writing a backlink into the pattern card, and what does such a link not establish?
Why can a visible backlog look stable while total work grows, and what must a stock-and-flow model do about stocks that sit outside its boundary?
Why does V12 keep a two-replication convergence-stress run that fails the 0.02 relative-error threshold instead of discarding it or reporting it as converged?
Why can a locally passing V12 validator not substitute for the V12-F review gate, and what does that gate still not establish?
Why is 'twenty requests per second of backlog' not a coherent state description, and what must be true before backlog divided by throughput can be read as a time?
Why can the V12 decision-validity gate not compensate for a failed statistical gate, and what outcome follows for a recommendation built on an unconverged run?
